messages:
Mia: Heads-up: planning to land the users.flags migration and follow-on backfill in prod tonight during the 23:00 UTC change window. Need coord on lock window and canary pinning.

deploy-bot: [notice] Scheduled deploy for migration 'users.add_flags_v2' queued for 2024-10-17T23:00:00Z. Canary target: user-service (2 instances).

Jonathan: quick check — how long is the exclusive lock expected? last run measured ~15s at peak but there were spikes.

Sofia: I ran it against staging with a snapshot of prod-ish traffic. Lock held ~12s median, 45s 99th. Backfill will do micro-batches to avoid hotspots.

Kevin: We should add a short drain: take one web node out of LB for canary, run migration, watch p99s for 5m, then proceed. Pin runtime to tag `user-service@2.14.1` for canary to avoid rolling platform changes.

Samir: +1 on pin. Also recommend setting DB_CONN_MAX to 200 for the window to avoid queueing. Ops doc: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/migrations#users-flags-backfill

Mia: ok agree. Plan: 23:00 UTC start, canary on one zone (pin 2.14.1), 10m observation, then gradual rollout 20%/50%/100% over 30m. Backfill micro-batch: 5k rows per txn, sleep 200ms between batches.

Jonathan: If we see lock > 60s or replication lag > 2m during canary, rollback immediately. What rollback looks like: revert svc pin and cancel backfill job; DB migration is safe to resume later because it uses transactional schema change + idempotent backfill marker.

Sofia: added a quick preflight script — run on prod read-replica to estimate locks and replication lag before we start. Command: ```bash
PGHOST=replica1 psql -c "SELECT * FROM pg_locks WHERE relation = 'users'::regclass AND mode LIKE '%Exclusive%';"
pg_stat_replication;
```

deploy-bot: [update] Preflight run queued. Use `/deploy preflight 1767890123 users.add_flags_v2` to attach results to this thread.

Kevin: Also flagging client SDKs — we'll include a short compatibility note in release notes for consumers using old user flags shape. Release notes draft: "Add optional user flags v2: backward-compatible; consumers should validate presence of new keys." Link: https://redwood.internal/releases/notes/2024-10-17-users-flags

Mia: During canary, if we see a 5% error bump or token cost spike, we stop and investigate. Who's oncall for DB? @Jonathan

Jonathan: I'm oncall. I'll monitor locks and replication. If we need to abort, post `abort-migration` and I'll run the rollback steps in the ops doc.

Samir: I'll own the backfill controller — can pause/resume jobs. I'll set thresholds: pause if txn retries > 3 for 5m or average latency > 300ms.

Mia: Great. Final checklist: pin service tag, preflight green, DB_CONN_MAX bump, canary one AZ, 10m observation, backfill controller armed, rollback criteria set. If all good we'll proceed at 23:00. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: [info] Migration 'users.add_flags_v2' will be executed at 2024-10-17T23:00:00Z. Use `/deploy cancel 1767890123` to cancel.
